newsitem.title: POLAND: Kredyt Bank bids for PBI, Prosper banks.
newsitem.headline: Kredyt Bank bids for PBI, Prosper banks.

text.p: The Polish bank Kredyt Bank SA placed bids for Polish Investment Bank SA (PBI) and Prosper Bank, now controlled by the central bank, Kredyt Bank said in a statement on Monday.
It said it was bidding for 100 percent of PBI shares and for 93 percent of Prosper.
Earlier on Monday the National Bank of Poland (NBP) said it planned to start talks next week with investors bidding for a strategic stake in PBI.

The NBP decided last year that it would offer PBI, carved out of the central bank in 1993 with a clean credit portfolio, together with the troubled smaller Prosper Bank it had taken over in a bail-out scheme.
Kredyt Bank's statement confirmed earlier media reports that it was bidding for PBI alongside Austria's Creditanstalt and GE Capital.
PBI, which was recently awarded a BBB- long-term rating by IBCA, had a net profit of 54.9 million zlotys last year against 26.2 million in 1995.
